name: Museum of the City of New York

collection_api.notes: Public collections portal at collections.mcny.org. Whether it exposes a machine-readable API, and whether accession lookup works against it, is UNVERIFIED — check before relying on it for ground truth.

accession_formats.policy: LOCATE, DO NOT VALIDATE. Five samples produced four different shapes. These patterns exist to help FIND the accession token on a label and to rank candidate readings. Nothing is ever rejected for failing them. See DECISIONS.md D11 and D21.

shapes.notes: X prefix. Often signals a loan, deposit or bulk-catalogued holding; here a LOOK magazine negative among many thousands. Longest and most fragile to OCR.

accession_formats.locating_heuristic: Last token on the credit line, optionally parenthesized. Digits and periods, optional leading letter. Do not constrain component count.

labels.note: MCNY uses at least two distinct label designs in one building. Select the parser by gallery, not by venue — see DECISIONS.md D10 and D11.

fields: title (+ date, inline or own line)
Photograph by NAME (+ optional object qualifier)
credit line + donation year + accession in parentheses
dialects.notes: No owning-institution line. Interpretive essay follows in both languages.

dialects.where: photography galleries, small white cards beside each print
field_order: institution + optional sub-collection + credit line + accession
dialects.notes: Classic §4.2 tombstone order — artist FIRST — unlike the black interpretive panels in the same department, which lead with the title. Two dialects coexist in one gallery.

labels.lighting: very dim; works behind glass with visible glare

access_rules.window_note: All opening hours that day. Unlike MoMA's Friday 17:30-20:30, there is no time restriction — so `window` must be optional in the model.

access_rules.recurrence_note: No temporal condition at all — so `recurrence` must also be optional. This rule and free-wednesdays exercise opposite ends of the model.

provenance.source: first-hand observation and the museum's own on-site signage, 2026-09-16
provenance.notes: Access rules read off the museum's own sandwich board at the entrance — per §8.2 the institution IS the authority on its own access policy, so this is a strong source. It is still a point-in-time reading of a movable sign, and §8.2's staleness clock applies: re-check against the museum's page rather than discounting it.
provenance.source_image_note: Bookend frames per D26. Both read by tools/ocr; the board (IMG_1287) yields the hours, the Wednesday rule, the three ZIP codes and the 104th St ramp verbatim. Neither carries GPS (camera permission was off that day).

hours.caveat: The board states Mon-Fri and Sat-Sun without naming a closed day. Open seven days is an INFERENCE from the absence of an exclusion, not something the sign asserts. Verify against the museum's own page before publishing.

accessibility.note: The Fifth Avenue entrance is up a flight of marble steps. Ramp and accessible entrance are around the corner on 104th Street. This is a REACHABILITY property of the venue (§6.6), distinct from any admission concession — the two are different facts and both are needed.

display_state_observations.observation: Building exterior under scaffolding and protective sheeting; facade renovation in progress.
display_state_observations.relevance: §8.3 — a feed reports what is scheduled, a sighting reports what is there. Construction can close galleries and no listings feed would say so. Exactly the class of fact only a visitor supplies.

display_state_observations.observation: Exhibitions advertised on the exterior: 'The Occupied City: New York and the American Revolution', 'Another Wonderland' (Champanier's Alice mural), and a third on Joe Macken's model.
display_state_observations.relevance: Corroborates the galleries the fixtures came from.
